1_inspection.architecture_found: provider_b_bridge.py is NOT an HTTP client to any Ollama endpoint (local or remote). It spawns its OWN independent `llama-server` subprocess (LLAMA_SERVER_BIN='/usr/local/lib/ollama/llama-server') which loads a GGUF model blob DIRECTLY FROM LOCAL DISK, resolved via Ollama's own on-disk manifest JSON (OLLAMA_MANIFEST_ROOT/OLLAMA_BLOB_ROOT, both hardcoded local filesystem paths). This is explicit, deliberate design (see the module's own docstring): 'a genuinely independent local inference provider... NOT dependent on the `ollama serve` daemon process... if `ollama serve` itself crashes or is stopped, this provider is unaffected' -- achieved specifically BY reading the model weights off local disk directly, bypassing any Ollama HTTP API entirely.

2_is_this_merely_an_incorrect_local_mani.reasoning: Two independent, compounding, genuinely architectural facts, not a logic bug in the availability-detection code: (1) This machine's llama-server binary at /usr/local/lib/ollama/llama-server does not exist at all (confirmed via `find / -iname llama-server` returning nothing, and `/usr/local/lib/ollama/` containing only GPU inference libraries -- libggml/CUDA v12+v13/vulkan -- no server binary). (2) This machine DOES run its own separate, real, local `ollama serve` process (confirmed live: PID present, http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags returns 200) -- but its installed model set (qwen2.5:1.5b, gemma2:2b, llama3:instruct, qwen2.5-coder:7b, deepseek-r1:8b, gemma:2b, gemma3:4b, qwen2.5:7b-instruct, nomic-embed-text) is completely disjoint from the engineering models Omni actually uses (qwen3-coder:30b, qwen3.6:27b, gpt-oss:20b), which live only on the remote GPU node (100.105.150.104) this machine reaches over Tailscale for its real engineering inference.

Provider B's entire value proposition (OLLAMA_SINGLE_PROVIDER_DEPENDENCY elimination) depends on genuine process-level independence, which requires the model weights and the inference binary to be co-located -- a requirement this machine cannot satisfy for the actual engineering models without either downloading the blob here (explicitly forbidden) or running llama-server on the remote GPU node instead (a materially different deployment/'installing another provider' elsewhere, also out of this campaign's explicit scope).
